raw_response:
I am old now, 67, so I do not want to spread myself too thin. My land is only 6 mu, and cash also has to be kept in hand. I have farmed here many years in Quzhou, so I mostly do what has worked on my own fields. Garlic needs more hand work but usually brings better money, so I keep that as the main crop on part of the land. After garlic comes out, I put maize in quickly, because that is the usual way here and it keeps the land earning. Wheat I still keep on the rest of the land for steady grain and because I know how to manage it. I have well water, so if spring is dry or the wheat and maize look thirsty, I will irrigate, but I will not water too many times because pumping costs money. I do not chase fancy methods. I use what is sold nearby, watch what neighbors do, and put fertilizer a bit on the safe side because if the crop turns yellow later, that loss is harder to bear than spending a little more now.

For garlic, I will not plant too much because it takes labor and my family members are not all at home. I will save some seed garlic if it looks healthy and buy the rest locally. For wheat, I follow the old habit: base fertilizer before sowing, then one topdress around jointing if the stand looks good enough. For maize after garlic, the time is tight, so I will do simple tillage and sow fast, not delay for perfect field preparation. I want a stable year, not the highest possible yield.
